artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.title: Limiting TE voting rights in presbytery and General Assembly to pastors

matches.evidence: The CCB again found the overture in conflict with BCO 3-1 and 14-2, reaffirming that restricting voting to pastors disenfranchises non-pastor Teaching Elders.

artifacts.title: Restricting presbytery and General Assembly voting to pastors only

matches.evidence: The CCB found the overture in conflict with BCO 3-1, which vests church power in the whole body, and BCO 14-2, which entitles all TEs to representation.

artifacts.title: Presbytery standing rule exempting retired ministers from reporting

matches.evidence: Illiana Presbytery's proposed rule relieving retired ministers from mandatory reporting was found not in conflict with BCO 23-2, with the presbytery advised to use its own wisdom under BCO 41-5.
